checkpoints.description: [1/2] Pin the untested review-lease ledger

impact_assessment.why: The idea-repo-review gap states the whole lease ledger has no tests; a grep confirmed zero references to release_expired, stale_reviews, reserved_ids, validate_reviews or _lease_expired in either tier. The lease decides which idea numbers parallel dossier sessions may claim, so an untested bug corrupts a shared register.
impact_assessment.benefits: Reservation, expiry, abandonment, idempotent release and forced takeover become pinned, so a later change cannot silently corrupt the register.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none, tests only; dependency: none (stdlib only); concurrency: none; state: tests/test_kit.py, the registry gap text, an ADR
impact_assessment.mitigation: write each pin from the implementation, correct any assumption the first run contradicts, keep the gap text to what remains true, and run both tiers plus every gate

[1/3] Make --audit create no directory when the ledger is absent

impact_assessment.why: run_disruption_audit calls get_ledger_path solely to compute a path when no ledger exists, and that helper unconditionally mkdirs the memory directory. Measured with --workspace on an empty dir: the audit creates .agents (empty). A read-only audit that writes a directory is an AX and DX defect: a probe, a health check or an agent's first look mutates the workspace it was asked to inspect.
impact_assessment.benefits: An absent ledger no longer causes a write, so any caller can probe a workspace without changing it; the quarantine-on-corrupt behaviour stays, because that is lossless recovery of damaged data.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: run_disruption_audit return values and the --audit CLI; dependency: none (stdlib only); concurrency: none; state: disruption_recovery.py, tests, an ADR
impact_assessment.mitigation: compute the path without the mkdir side effect instead of changing get_ledger_path itself, which write paths rely on; pin both the absent-ledger and corrupt-ledger cases; run both tiers and every gate

[1/3] Add a reverse lookup from a bare state name to the machines that own it

impact_assessment.why: 88 distinct state names exist across 21 machines and 19 of them are shared (absent in five machines, missing in four). An agent holding a bare status string read from a JSON file has no way to learn which machine it belongs to: --check-status requires --machine, so the name must already be known. Measured: --check-status killed exits 2 with 'requires --machine'.
impact_assessment.benefits: An agent can resolve a status it found in the wild to the machine that defines it, and see every machine when the name is shared; this is the discoverability half P12 asked for without duplicating vocabularies into twenty help texts.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: state_machines.py CLI gains one flag, existing flags unchanged; dependency: none (stdlib only); concurrency: none; state: state_machines.py, tests, the doc, an ADR
impact_assessment.mitigation: additive flag only; unknown state still exits 1 like --check-status; pin shared-name and unknown-name cases; run both tiers and every gate

[1/3] proof_envelope.verify crashed on a non-object envelope instead of returning the inconclusive verdict it documents

impact_assessment.why: verify() documents 'fail-closed, never raises', and has an explicit isinstance guard whose message says 'envelope is not a JSON object'. The guard calls refused(), which read envelope.get('keyid') before the guard applied, so a JSON array, string, number or null raised AttributeError. Measured through the CLI: `proof_envelope.py verify arr.json` exited 1 with a traceback, not [INCONCLUSIVE].
impact_assessment.benefits: A malformed envelope now produces the documented inconclusive verdict with the Why/Fix triad, so an agent sees a verdict instead of a stack trace and the fail-closed contract is true rather than aspirational.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: verify() return shape unchanged for valid mappings, and the new keyid is None for a non-object; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: proof_envelope.py, one test
impact_assessment.mitigation: one-line defensive shaped mapping; the new test covers list/str/int/None; every existing envelope test still passes

checkpoints.description: [3/3] refused() reads keyid from a shaped mapping; non-object envelope now returns inconclusive with a null keyid; 1 fail-first test, 6 TestProofEnvelope pass, 1035 unit + 89 integration green; all gates incl dogfood 5/5 and budget

[1/3] proof_corpus store and proof_gate --receipt crash under their documented `python scripts/<module>.py` invocation

impact_assessment.why: Both write_receipt/_atomic_write_json import `scripts.disruption_recovery` unconditionally. Under `python scripts/proof_corpus.py` the scripts directory is sys.path[0] and the package root is not, so the import raises ModuleNotFoundError. Measured: `proof_corpus.py store valid.json --corpus c` exited 1 with a traceback, and `write_receipt` raised ModuleNotFoundError under the same import layout. Both modules already use a dual fallback for evidence_outcome, so the intended pattern is script-mode safe.
impact_assessment.benefits: Both documented CLIs work as printed in their own --help and `prog`, so an agent following the usage line no longer gets a stack trace after a successful proof. It also makes the existing dual-import pattern consistent across all three lazy imports.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: unchanged in package mode, sibling fallback only on ImportError; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: both modules, two tests, an ADR
impact_assessment.mitigation: fallback only on ImportError; two hermetic tests that simulate script mode by clearing the package entry; each proven to error on the old code

[1/2] Preserve a manual UI identity across fix and media init (P9)

impact_assessment.why: auto_ui called detect_ui(respect_manual=False) and wrote unconditionally, so `fix` and `media init` discarded a human's `ui-id --set yes|no`. The pinned test tests/test_kit.py test_ui_identity_can_be_set_manually_and_reported asserts auto_ui() with no argument overwrites, which is the correct meaning for `ui-id --set auto`; the defect is that maintenance callers used the same unconditional path. Measured: after a manual identity, `fix` rewrote ui_source=detected.
impact_assessment.benefits: A human's explicit UI decision survives routine repair, so the recorded identity matches what the user chose; `ui-id --set auto` keeps its documented overwrite so an agent can still force a re-detect.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: auto_ui and adopt_ui gain a keyword-only respect_manual defaulting to False, so every existing caller and the pinned test are unchanged; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: project_ui.py, aikit_cli.py, two tests
impact_assessment.mitigation: default False preserves the pinned overwrite; fix and media init pass True; three tests (direct auto_ui, fix via CLI, and the existing pinned test) prove both directions

[1/2] Harden two more JSON readers that crash on a non-object document

impact_assessment.why: sync_licenses.check_licenses (the default --check action) and dossier_sync._upsert_jsonld (the publish hook) call .get on json.loads output without checking it is an object. sync_licenses already guards the inner sha256 value but not the pin itself; dossier_sync guards nothing. Measured: check_licenses raised AttributeError for a JSON array/string/number/null/bool PIN.json, and _upsert_jsonld raised AttributeError('list' object has no attribute 'get') for a hand-edited JSON-LD array.
impact_assessment.benefits: A corrupt pinned copy surfaces as a named finding and a malformed dossier graph is skipped, so a read-only license audit and a publish report instead of leaving a traceback.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: check_licenses already returns list[str] and _upsert_jsonld already returns bool on every other path, so the shapes are unchanged; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: two modules, two tests
impact_assessment.mitigation: guard at the boundary before any .get; each test covers every non-object JSON shape and was proven to raise on the old code; existing license and dossier tests must still pass
